newsitem.title: FINLAND: FOCUS - AAMULEHTI PLANS FINNISH MEDIA MAJOR.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - AAMULEHTI PLANS FINNISH MEDIA MAJOR.

text.p: Finnish media group Aamulehti, facing increasingly stiff competition from its local rival Sanoma Oy, said on Tuesday it would merge with domestic commercial broadcaster MTV Oy to create a new media major.
"By combining two ... strong communications experts, we create a significant media group also on a European scale," Aamlulehti Oy CEO Matti Packalen said in a statement.

Packalen told a news conference talks had started in early spring, but the news came just days after Aamulehti's chief print rival, Sanoma which publishes leading national daily Helsingin Sanomat, said it planned a major expansion into electronic and print business news.
That would be a direct rival to Aamulehti's Kauppalehti business daily, which has to date dominated the business news market in print.

Aamulehti said the new bourse-listed company, to be created in 1998, would have net annual sales around 2.5 billion markka and 2,600 full-time employees -- more than the 1.8 billion markka net sales and 1,740 staff at Sanoma in 1996.
The new company would have a strong market share in the print, electronic and audiovisual sectors and be a front-runner in the area of new media and digital technology, it said.
"This newly signed agreement is an answer to many open questions about the future of the Finnish communication business," Packalen said in the statement.
"The aim is to make sure that we can meet all the challenges to come," he told the news conference.

Aamulehti also publishes a leading tabloid newspaper, Iltalehti; it is already active in radio, and several of its publications have moved into electronic real-time publishing, including on the Internet.
The merging companies said they had both had strong earnings in recent years and the merger would guarantee strength in the balance sheet and profitability from the start.
"The new listed company will be a diversified media group which should interest international investors too," Packalen said in the statement.
Pending approval by the authorities for the deal, Aamulehti shares would be converted into the new company's shares at one-to-one with shares in MTV converted at one to 137.5.

Aamulehti's biggest current shareholder is Swedish media group Marieberg Tidnings Ab , with 27.1 percent. Packalen told the news conference he understood Marieberg would target a 20 percent holding in the new company.
